summary: Delphine Menant (1850–1932) worked in Indology and religious studies. She studied under James Darmesteter and was appointed chargée de mission dans l’Inde at the Guimet Museum in 1900.
Demchok Dorje was a scholar who studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Denis Sinor (1916–2011) specialized in linguistics, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Paul Pelliot (~1939–1944) and at Cambridge (~1948), later holding posts at Cambridge (1948–1962) and Indiana University Bloomington (1962–1986).

Denis Twitchett (1925–2006) was a scholar of Sinology and history. Educated at SOAS and St Catharine's College, Cambridge, he held chairs of Chinese at the University of London (1960–1968) and Cambridge (1968–1980), later serving at Princeton University (1980–1994).

Denise Bernot (1922–2016) worked in linguistics and related fields. She studied at the École des chartes and École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1947–1950), and taught at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1960–1989).

Denma Lochö Rinpoche (1928–2014) was a Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology scholar. Educated at Drepung Loseling Monastery and Gyume Tantric College under multiple masters, he served as principal of the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics and Abbot of Namgyal Monastery (1986–1991).

Dennis A. Johnson specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2012) and held a post at the university's South Asian, Tibetan and Buddhist Studies Library (attested 2022).

Dennis Genpo Merzel (born 1944) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Southern California and the USC Rossier School of Education, and trained under Taizan Maezumi (~1972–1995).

Dennis Hirota (born 1946) works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at UC Berkeley and Nagoya University (Ph.D.). He held professorial posts at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2001) and Ryukoku University (2014), and visited Harvard in 2008.
Denys de Saumarez Bray (1875–1951) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Balliol College, Oxford (~1894–1898) and served as a Member of the Council of India from 1930 to 1937.

Denzaburo Yoshizawa (1924–2003) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji (~1946–1949). He held academic posts at Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1953–1987) and Iryo Sosei University.
Denzil Ibbetson (1847–1908) was an Indology scholar who studied at St Peter's College, Adelaide, and completed a B.A. in mathematics at St John's College (~1865–1869).
Deocar Schmid (1791–1828) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied theology at the University of Jena (1808–1813) and studied under Carl Christian Erhard Schmid.

Derek F. Maher is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his M.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, held lectureships at Virginia and UNC Greensboro, and co-directed East Carolina University's Religious Studies Program (attested 2010).

Dermot Killingley (born 1935) specializes in Indology and religious studies. Educated at Oxford, Merton College, and SOAS under David Friedman and Arnold Kunst, he held posts at the University of Malaya (1961–1968) and Newcastle University (~1970–2000).

Dermott Walsh specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Trinity College Dublin (BA), Leiden University (MA), and the University of California, Los Angeles (PhD, 2018), where his doctoral supervisor was William M. Bodiford.

Dessislava Vendova is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar educated at Sofia, BLCU, Peking, Columbia, and Kyoto universities. Her posts include fellow at Graduate Theological Union (2020–2023) and appointments at Boston MFA, UMass Boston (2025), and Holy Cross (2025).

Detlef Ingo Lauf (1936–2001) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held professorships at the C. G. Jung Institute Zürich, the California Institute of Integral Studies, Ohio University, and Columbia Pacific University.

Devachandra Bharati 'Prakhar' is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who has served as a research scholar and pursued doctoral studies at Mahatma Jyotiba Phule Rohilkhand University (2021–2026).

Devadatta Ramakrishna Bhandarkar (1875–1950) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Superintendent of the Archaeological Survey of India's Western Circle (1911–1917) and Carmichael Professor at the University of Calcutta (attested 1910).
